parties:
Abdul Jalil ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Steel & Engineering Corporation having its office at "Steel House" Kawran Bazar, Police Station Tejgaon, Dhaka and others ----- Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.: This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner Abdul Jalil was issued calling upon the defendant opposite parties, (1) Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation, PS Tejgaon, Dhaka, (2) Chairman, Bangladesh Steel & Engineering Corporation hereinafter called BSEC, (3) Secretary, BSEC and (4) Chief Personnel Officer, BSEC to show cause why the judgment and decree passed by Mr. Quamrul Islam Siddique, Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 301/83 on 29.6.85 and the judgment and decree passed by Mr. Md. Ali Khan, Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 163/85 on 29.2.88 should not be set aside. 

 2. On 28th July, 1983 plaintiff Abdul Jalil instituted Title Suit No. 301/83 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, stating that he was appointed in the former East Pakistan Industries Development Corporation as a Metallurigical Engineer, Iron & Steel Works, Chittagong on 4.6.66 by an appointment letter issued by the predecessor of defendant No. 3 (that is the secretary of the then EPIDC) mainly on condition that he will be on probation for six months at the first instance and on completion of his probation his services will be placed on 5 years' contract with effect from commencement of his appointment and further extension of contract will be with mutual agreement. After completion of probation his services were placed on 5 years contract with effect from 7.10.66 by defendant No. 3, Secretary's letter dated 28.4.69. Thereafter on the expiry of two more consecutive five-year term contracts with effect from 7.10.71 and 7.10.76 the contract for a further period of 5 years was made by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with the plaintiff with effect from 7.10.81 by letter dated 4.9.81. The plaintiff petitioner had become the General Manager (Steel) BSEC, Dhaka in 1977 and in 1981 he was Managing Director, Chittagong Steel Mills Ltd. North Patenga, Chittagong. In the matter of running and management of the Chittagong Steel Mills there arose some misunderstanding between the plaintiff and defendant No. 2, the Chairman, The plaintiff protested against some of the actions of defendant No. 2 which, according to the plaintiff, were detremental to the Mill itself. Out of grudge defendant No. 2, the Chairman, BSEC got the letter dated 20.4.83 issued to the effect that as per decision of the Board of Directors the plaintiff (MA Jalil, General Manager (Steel), BSEC Dhaka) is put under suspension with immediate effect and that during the suspension period he will be entitled to get suspension allowances as per Rules. Thereafter the plaintiff wrote the letter dated 2nd May, 1983 to the Chairman, Bangladesh Steel & Engineering Corporation, wanting to know why he has been placed under suspension and whether it was because of their disagreement of the issue of importing 28 gauge CI sheet for the Chittagong Steel Mill. He also stated in the said letter that the order putting him on suspension was illegal and malicious. Thereafter by a letter dated 2.5.83 defendant No. 3, Secretary, BSEC communicated the charge of misconduct to the plaintiff by a special messenger asking him to show cause within 7 days of the receipt of the letter. The plaintiff by his letter dated 8th May, 1983 replied to the charge. The defendants sent another letter dated 19.5.83 to the plaintiff to enquire into the charge and the plaintiff sent a reply to the said letter dated 19.5.83. The Board of Directors of the Bangladesh Steel & Engineering Corporation dismissed the plaintiff on the grounds stated by the Board and the decision of the Board was communicated to the plaintiff by defendant No. 3, the Secretary of the BSEC by letter dated 21.6.83 containing the reasons for dismissal of the plaintiff. According to the plaintiff, the order of dismissal passed by defendant No. 2 under the signature of defendant No. 3 is illegal, inoperative, void and against the principle of natural justice. The said dismissal was done with a motive to give a stigma to the good name and reputation of the plaintiff as on officer. The cause of action of the case arose on 21.6.83 when the plaintiff was dismissed from the service of the Corporation by the defendants. The plaintiff prayed for the following reliefs : 

 3. The defendants filed a joint written statement on 5.3.84. The case for the defendants is that the plaintiff at the relevant time was an employee of defendant No. 1 which is a statutory corporation under PO No. 27/72 read with Ordinance No.XXV/76. The plaintiff at that time was serving as a General Manager (Steel) under the defendant No. 1. The defendant No. 2 is the Chairman of Defendant No. 1, Defendant No. 4 is the Chief Personnel Officer of Defendant No. 1. On 27.4.83 defendant No. 2 gave certain directive to the plaintiff to coordinate and facilitate removal of the finished stock & raw materials from the Re-rolling Mills under disinvestment and which arc to be handed over to the purchasers within a very short time by taking up the matter with NBR, Banks and other agencies involved in the process on priority basis in consultation with Accounts and Marketing Division. He advised the plaintiff to visit the GM Steel, Chittagong Steel Mill Ltd. both located at Chittagong in order to ensure that specified type of bars were supplied to the Power Development Board without any further delay. Defendant No. 2 also instructed the plaintiff to know about the shipment of Chittagong Steel Mill. On the following day, i.e. 25.4.83 at about 12-30 PM the defendant No. 2 called the plaintiff and Mr. S Hyder, General Manager in his chamber and asked the plaintiff about the progress made on the work assigned to the plaintiff on the previous day. At that time the Director (Finance), Chief Personnel Officer and the Acting General Manager were also present in the office chamber of defendant No. 2. The said defendant No. 2 (the Chairman) repeatedly asked the plaintiff to let him to know about the progress of the said work. The plaintiff kept silent for some time without giving any reply. At long last the plaintiff replied -in rough and rude manner that he would not reply to the Chairman's directive orders or instructions. Defendant No. 2 and everyone present there were surprised on such reply given by the plaintiff. When the defendant No. 2 Chairman told the plaintiff that if he disobeys his orders, he would render himself liable to disciplinary action, the plaintiff got more infuriated and then jumped up in his chair and shouted at defendant No. 2. The plaintiff took up a paper weight in his hand and started moving towards the defendant No. 2 saying that he would kill defendant No. 2. When the plaintiff made an attempt to assault defendant No. 2 with the said paper weight the Officers present there quickly intervened and stopped the plaintiff asking him to refrain from inflicting any physical injury on defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 2 got frightened at such behavior of the plaintiff and out of fear he went to the corner of his chamber keeping a safe distance. The plaintiff was still then very angry and shouted that he would kill defendant No. 2 and that if he could not kill deft. 2 on that date, he would kill him in future. Thereafter the plaintiff left the chamber of defendant No. 2 in an angry mood hurling abuses towards defendant No. 2. Thereafter a special meeting of the Board of Directors was held on the same date i.e. on 24.8.83 in which the entire matter and the incident were discussed. It was prima facie found that the behavior of the plaintiff was an act of gross misconduct calling for taking disciplinary action, suspension and drawing up of disciplinary proceedings. The plaintiff was put under suspension by the Board of Directors by Office Order dated 28.4.83 to the effect that as per decision of the Board of Directors, Mr. MA Jalil (plaintiff) General Manager (Steel), BSEC, Dhaka was put under suspension with immediate effect and that during the suspension period he would be entitled to get subsistence allowance as per Rules. The Office Order of the Board of Directors was signed by defendant No. 4, the Chief Personnel Officer. Thereafter the plaintiff was charged for misconduct as per office Order dated 2.5.83, Ext. 6, detailing the allegations 1st the plaintiff who was asked to show cause thin seven days of the receipt of the said letter containing the charge as to why on the said ground he should not be dismissed from the service or otherwise suitably punished for committing the act of misconduct stated therein. It was further ordered that suspension was to continue until final decision of his case or until further order. The plaintiff submitted his explanation dated 8.5.83 in reply to the charges leveled against him which was not satisfactory to the Board of Directors which then constituted a Committee of Enquiry consisting of two members, namely, (1) Mr. AEA Monim (General Manager, Engg. III), BACC and (2) Mr. GM Khan, General Manager (Purchase) BSEC. The order was communicated to the plaintiff by Office Order dated 12.5.83 and was signed by defendant No. 3, the Secretary. The two members of the Enquiry Committee under their own signatures sent a letter dated 19.5.83, Ext. A, by Special Messenger to the plaintiff informing him that they as members of the Enquiry Committee have been asked to investigate into the charges against the plaintiff and to submit report thereon and that therefore, the plaintiff should appear before the Enquiry Committee with evidence and witnesses on his behalf on 23.5.83 at 10-00 AM in the Board Room of the BSEC, Steel House, Kawran Bazar, Dhaka for enquiry into the said charges. Even after receiving this notice the plaintiff did not turn up before the Enquiry Committee at the aforesaid place on 23.5.83 at all. The said two members of the Enquiry Committee thereafter by their letter dated 31.5.83, Ext. A(1), informed the plaintiff that although he was requested to appear before the Enquiry Committee on 23.5.83 in the Board Room of BSEC Steel House, Kawran Bazar, Dhaka for enquiry into the charges against him and although he received the said letter on 19.5.83 yet he did not turn up on 23.5.83 without intimation to the Enquiry Committee, that the Enquiry Committee for the ends of justice adjourned the enquiry and that in order to give the plaintiff a further chance to appear before the Enquiry Committee they have fixed 5.6.83 as the next date of enquiry on which date he should appear before the Board at 10-00 AM with his evidence and witnesses for enquiry into the aforesaid charges of misconduct. The two members of the Committee also intimated the plaintiff by the said letter, Ext. A(1) dated 31.5.83 that if he fails to turn up on 5.6.83 in time, the enquiry will proceed ex parse without any further reference to him. The said letter was sent by Special Messenger and the plaintiff received said letter on the same date. It appears that in reply to the Enquiry Committee's letter dated 19.5.83, Ext. A, the plaintiff sent his letter dated 19.5.83, Ext. B, to defendant No. 2, the Chairman to the effect that he had received the letter dated 19.5.83, Ext. A, signed by Mr. Momin and Mr. GM Khan, the two members of the enquiry committee asking him to appear before the Enquiry Committee on 23.5.83 at 10-00 AM in BSEC Board Room, that he had already submitted reply to defendant No. 2's charges on 8.5.83, that defendant No. 2 should either accept the charges leveled against him (defendant No. 2) by the plaintiff or refute the charges brought by the plaintiff against defendant No. 2, that defendant No. 2 was trying to cancel the remaining portion of his contract to serve defendant No. 2's own interest, that his 5 year's contract service as Managing Director of the Chittagong Steel Mill will expire on 6.10.86 and that under these circumstances he has nothing to add to what has been already said in his reply dated 8.5.83, Ext. 5. The plaintiff did not appear before the Enquiry Committee even on the second opportunity to defend himself on 5.6.83 in the BSEC Board Room and the Enquiry Committee proceeded to examine witnesses ex pane. On 5.6.83 the Enquiry Committee examined defendant No. 2, the Chairman Mr. Nazrul Islam (his statement marked as Ext. H), Mr. S Ryder (his statement marked as Ext. 1-1(1) and Dr. AS Nuriddin (Chief Personnel Officer) (his statement marked as H(2). On 6.6.83 the Enquiry Committee examined Mr. AF Mutajid, Acting General Manager (Planning) (his statement marked as Ext. H-3) Mr. S Murtaza Hossain, Director (Finance), BSEC (his statement marked Ext. H-4) was examined by the Enquiry Committee on 7.6.83. The Enquiry Committee submitted report (Ext. G) regarding their enquiry under their signatures dated 14.6.83 to the Board of Directors analysing the evidence of the witnesses and made the following finding : "On the analysis of the statements of the witnesses and charges disclosed therein the charges made against Mr. Abdul Jalil have been established beyond any reasonable doubt that Mr. Abdul Jalil had committed (a) act of gross insubordination and flouting of official orders, instructions. (b) attempted to assault the Chairman with a paper weight and (on these grounds) he has been found guilty of charges (of misconduct and insubordination) which call for appropriate disciplinary action against him." 

 6. The learned Subordinate Judge found that the suit is not barred by limitation. The learned Subordinate Judge relying on the decision in the case of Md. Lutful Kabir Vs. Secretary, Agaz Rubber Industries Ltd., 29 DLR 45 held that the employee of a corporation not being an employee of the Government, relationship between them will be one of master and servant and further relying on the decision reported in 19 DLR 307 held that the plaintiff being an employee under a corporate body cannot sue against dismissal with a prayer for a declaration that his dismissal order is wrong, inoperative and void on the ground that except in the suit for damages for compensation, no other suit would lick nor the servant is entitled to any other relief such as reinstatement to service or to a mere declaration that the servant was wrongfully terminated by the master. On this ground the learned Subordinate Judge held that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. He further found that there is absolutely no substance in the argument of the learned advocate for the plaintiff that the plaintiff did not get adequate chance of being heard and also observed that plaintiff himself deposed that he received the notice and that he was asked to appear before the Enquiry Committee. The plaintiff further deposed he replied to the notice also and that he also received the second notice to attend the Enquiry to defend himself. So he deliberately avoided attending the enquiry proceedings. So it is clear that the plaintiff was given all possible chances of being heard. Relying on the decision of Manager Personnel Division Vs. Md. Shajahan reported in 35 DLR 224, the learned Subordinate Judge held that the question of violating the principle of natural justice does not arise when the person concerned has been dismissed after affording him an opportunity to defend himself. On this ground also he dismissed the plaintiff's suit. 

 10. Mr. Abdul Hamid Chowdhury, learned Advocate for the plaintiff appellant, argued that the defendants should have served a second show cause notice before dismissing or removing him from service. We are unable to find any substance in such argument in view of the fact that the principle of natural justice requires only an opportunity to be given to defend himself and that the principle of natural justice does not automatically give to the affected person a right to second show cause notice unless such a provision is in the service rules or in the Parent Act. Undisputedly the plaintiff is not a Government servant. He was an employee of the Corporation under a contract. In the case of Manager Personnel Division Vs. Md. Shajahan Mia, 35 DLR 224 it has been rightly held, "The plaintiff has alleged that the bank did not cause the issuance of a second show cause notice before the dismissal and that the plaintiff was deprived of natural justice. So far as the principle of second show cause notice is concerned, this was constitutional protection available to persons holding any civil post under the Republic and not to any employee of any statutory authority in the absence of any provision in that Act or Rules of such statutory authority. The principle of natural justice must be found to have been duly complied with if it becomes evident that the plaintiff was dismissed from service after affording him an opportunity to defend himself from the charges leveled against him. When that was done admittedly, there was no cause for finding that the principle of natural justice was not complied with."
